q: In what year was the BCS (British Computer Society) founded?
explain: BCS (British computer society) founded 1957; approx. 100,000 members.

q: Approximately how many members does the IET have, according to the slides?
explain: IET: founded in 2006, approx. 150,000 members.

explain: BCS: founded 1957; approx. 100,000 members.

explain: ACM founded 1947; approx. 75,000 members.

q: What does ACM stand for, as written on the slide?

options: Institute for Embedded and Electronic Engineering
Institute for Electrical and Electronic Engineers

q: What does CPD stand for in the context of protecting yourself as a professional?
explain: Slide 16 refers to support for Continuing Professional Development; slide 12 lists CPD as a way to protect yourself as a professional.

q: How does the lecture define professionalism?
options: Having a legal duty to act in an emergency
Maintaining an ethical approach to one's job within the structure of an association
explain: Professionalism is maintaining an ethical approach to one's job within the structure of an association (Adams & McCrindle, 2008).

q: Who said: 'The public are entitled to expect that the same professional disciplines apply in IT as in other professions such as medicine and law'?
explain: Quote attributed to Roger Johnson, BCS President.

q: Which of the following is named as a way to protect yourself as a professional?
explain: How do you protect yourself as a professional? Professional indemnity insurance; CPD.

q: Which of the following is listed by Bott (2014) as a profession?
explain: Bott (2014) describes professions as including doctors, lawyers, accountants, architects, IT professionals. Trades are posed as a question (s4).

q: According to Bott's common features of professions, who decides the nature of training and controls entry to the profession?
explain: The professional bodies themselves decide the nature of training and control entry to the profession.

q: How many main sections does the BCS Code of Conduct have on the slides?
explain: 1 Public Interest, 2 Professional Competence and Integrity, 3 Duty to Relevant Authority, 4 Duty to the Profession.

q: Which BCS Code of Conduct section covers 'accept professional responsibility for your work'?
explain: 3. Duty to Relevant Authority: ... accept professional responsibility for your work.

q: Which BCS Code of Conduct section covers 'reject and will not make any offer of bribery or unethical inducement'?
explain: 2. Professional Competence and Integrity: ... reject and will not make any offer of bribery or unethical inducement.

q: Which BCS Code of Conduct section covers 'promote equal access to the benefits of IT'?
explain: 1. Public Interest: promote equal access to the benefits of IT.

q: Which BCS Code of Conduct section covers 'uphold the reputation and good standing of BCS'?
explain: 4. Duty to the Profession: ... uphold the reputation and good standing of BCS, the Chartered Institute for IT.

q: To whom does the BCS Code of Conduct apply?
options: All members, irrespective of their membership grade
Only members working in the UK
explain: Applies to all members, irrespective of their membership grade.

q: Under the BCS Code of Conduct, when may you disclose confidential information?
options: With the permission of your Authority, or as required by Legislation
Whenever the public asks for it
explain: You shall NOT disclose, or use for personal gain, confidential information except with the permission of your Authority, or as required by Legislation.

q: Which of the following is NOT something that defines a professional body?
options: Issuing a Code of Conduct, or ethics
Setting the price of its members' services
explain: Slide 16 lists the defining features; setting prices is not among them.

q: Which body is described as a 'not-for-profit charity that promotes web security'?
explain: OWASP: not-for-profit charity that promotes web security.

q: Which body is described as an 'International not-for-profit accreditation and certification body'?
explain: CREST: International not-for-profit accreditation and certification body.

q: Which body is described as a 'manufacturer and certification body'?
explain: CISCO: manufacturer and certification body.

q: Which ACM Code of Ethics item says to 'access computing and communication resources only when authorized or when compelled by the public good'?
explain: ACM professional responsibilities: Access computing and communication resources only when authorized or when compelled by the public good.

q: Which ACM Code of Ethics item is a general ethical principle (rather than a professional responsibility)?
options: Accept and provide appropriate professional review
Design and implement systems that are robustly and usably secure
Perform work only in areas of competence
explain: General ethical principles include 'Avoid harm'; the others are professional responsibilities.

q: Under the BCS Code of Conduct, you shall NOT:
options: Seek, accept and offer honest criticisms of work
Claim any level of competence that you do not possess
Develop your knowledge on a continuing basis
Comply with Legislation relevant to your work
explain: NOT claim any level of competence that you do not possess.

q: According to the slides, which is the closing guidance on health and safety?
options: Health and safety is optional for IT professionals
explain: Health and Safety: ... Common sense should prevail.

q: According to Bott (2014), what do professions have in common?
options: Government decides who may enter the profession
The profession is organised into one or more professional bodies
Members are paid above the national average
Members are expected to conduct activities in accordance with codes of conduct laid out by the professional bodies
The professional bodies decide the nature of training and control entry to the profession
Substantial education and training in order to practise
explain: Slide 3 lists the four things in common.

options: Membership of an overseeing body to be able to practice
Skills are in short supply, or difficult to obtain

q: Which of the following make a job a profession?
explain: Slide 8: self regulation, agreed body of shared knowledge, certifications or examinations.

q: Which of the following are listed as results of having a profession?
options: Safer supply of service to the public
explain: Slide 9 lists these (as questions).

q: What defines a professional body?
options: Dealing with complaints against professionals and implementing disciplinary procedures
Issuing a Code of Conduct, or ethics, to guide professional behaviour
explain: Slide 16.

q: What defines a professional body?
options: Provide professional networks to meet and discuss their field
Enable fairer access to the professions
Provide careers support and opportunities for students, graduates and people already working
explain: Slide 16.

q: Which statements about the BCS Code of Conduct are correct?
options: It governs the conduct of employers
It sets the professional standards required as a condition of membership
It applies only to chartered members
It applies to all members, irrespective of their membership grade
It governs the conduct of the individual
explain: BCS (The Chartered Institute for IT) Code of Conduct: slide 17.

q: Under 'Public Interest', what shall a BCS member do?
options: Have due regard for public health, privacy, security and wellbeing of others and the environment
Promote equal access to the benefits of IT
Only undertake work within professional competence
Seek to avoid conflict of interest with their Authority
Have due regard for the legitimate rights of Third Parties
explain: Slide 18. The last two belong to other sections.

q: Under 'Professional Competence and Integrity', what shall a BCS member do?
options: Uphold the reputation and good standing of BCS
Only undertake work that is within their professional competence
Develop their professional knowledge, skills and competence on a continuing basis
Avoid injuring others, their property, reputation, or employment by false or malicious or negligent action or inaction
Reject and not make any offer of bribery or unethical inducement
Ensure they have knowledge and understanding of Legislation and comply with it
Respect and value alternative viewpoints and seek, accept and offer honest criticisms of work

q: Under 'Duty to Relevant Authority', what shall a BCS member do?
options: Seek to improve professional standards through participation in their development
Promote the inclusion of all sectors in society
Not misrepresent or withhold information on the performance of products, systems or services
Carry out professional responsibilities with due care and diligence
Accept professional responsibility for their work
Seek to avoid any situation that may give rise to a conflict of interest with their Authority
explain: Slide 20. The last two belong to Duty to the Profession and Public Interest.

q: Under 'Duty to the Profession', what shall a BCS member do?
options: Accept professional responsibility for their work
Accept their personal duty to uphold the reputation of the profession
Uphold the reputation and good standing of BCS
Act with integrity and respect in professional relationships with all members of BCS and members of other professions
Seek to improve professional standards through participation in their development, use and enforcement
explain: Slide 21. The last two belong to Duty to Relevant Authority and Professional Competence and Integrity.

q: On which grounds does the BCS Code of Conduct say you must not discriminate?
explain: Without discrimination on the grounds of sex, sexual orientation, marital status, nationality, colour, race, ethnic origin, religion, age or disability, or of any other condition or requirement.

Be fair and take action not to discriminate
Respect the work required to produce new ideas, inventions, creative works, and computing artefacts

q: Which of the following are ACM professional responsibilities?
options: Design and implement systems that are robustly and usably secure
Be fair and take action not to discriminate
Accept and provide appropriate professional review
Know and respect existing rules pertaining to professional work
Strive to achieve high quality in both the processes and products of professional work
Perform work only in areas of competence
